Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.name: Bell Pepper Bacterial Spot
Pepper__bell___Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease (Xanthomonas) that spreads in warm, wet weather and damages leaves and fruit.
symptoms: Small, dark, water-soaked spots on leaves
Spots turning brown with yellow edges
treatment: Remove and destroy infected plant parts
Use copper-based sprays as advised by a local agriculture expert

Pepper__bell___healthy.name: Healthy Bell Pepper Leaf
Pepper__bell___healthy.description: The leaf shows no visible signs of disease.
treatment: No treatment needed
prevention: Water at the base of the plant
Keep the area free of plant debris

Potato___Early_blight.name: Potato Early Blight
Potato___Early_blight.description: A fungal disease (Alternaria solani) that mainly affects older leaves.
treatment: Remove affected leaves
Apply a suitable fungicide as advised locally
prevention: Keep plants well fed and healthy

Potato___Late_blight.name: Potato Late Blight
Potato___Late_blight.description: A fast-spreading disease (Phytophthora infestans) favoured by cool, humid weather.
symptoms: White fuzzy growth under leaves in humid weather
Rapid browning of leaves and stems
treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants quickly
Use recommended fungicides as advised locally

Potato___healthy.name: Healthy Potato Leaf
Potato___healthy.description: The leaf shows no visible signs of disease.
treatment: No treatment needed

Tomato_Bacterial_spot.name: Tomato Bacterial Spot
Tomato_Bacterial_spot.description: A bacterial disease that thrives in warm, wet conditions and affects leaves and fruit.
symptoms: Small, dark, greasy-looking spots on leaves
treatment: Remove infected leaves
Use copper-based sprays as advised locally

Tomato_Early_blight.name: Tomato Early Blight
Tomato_Early_blight.description: A fungal disease (Alternaria solani) that starts on the lower, older leaves.
symptoms: Dark sunken spots on stems or fruit
treatment: Remove affected lower leaves
Apply a suitable fungicide as advised locally
prevention: Water at the base of the plant

Tomato_Late_blight.name: Tomato Late Blight
Tomato_Late_blight.description: A fast-spreading disease (Phytophthora infestans) that thrives in cool, wet weather.
symptoms: White fuzzy growth under leaves in humid conditions
treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants
Apply a recommended fungicide as advised locally

Tomato_Leaf_Mold.name: Tomato Leaf Mold
Tomato_Leaf_Mold.description: A fungal disease (Passalora fulva) common in humid, poorly ventilated conditions.
symptoms: Pale yellow patches on the upper leaf surface
Olive-green to brown mold under the leaf
treatment: Remove infected leaves
Reduce humidity and apply a suitable fungicide as advised locally

Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.name: Tomato Septoria Leaf Spot
Tomato_Septoria_leaf_spot.description: A fungal disease (Septoria lycopersici) that spreads by water splash.
symptoms: Many small round spots with dark borders and grey centres
Yellowing and dropping of lower leaves
treatment: Remove affected leaves
Apply a suitable fungicide as advised locally
prevention: Rotate crops and clear plant debris

Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.name: Tomato Spider Mites
Tomato_Spider_mites_Two_spotted_spider_m.description: Tiny pests that suck sap from leaves, most active in hot, dry weather.
symptoms: Tiny yellow or white speckles on leaves
Leaves turning bronze and drying out
treatment: Spray leaves with water to knock mites off
Use insecticidal soap or miticide as advised locally
prevention: Check the underside of leaves regularly

Tomato__Target_Spot.name: Tomato Target Spot
Tomato__Target_Spot.description: A fungal disease (Corynespora cassiicola) favoured by warm, humid weather.
treatment: Remove affected leaves
Apply a suitable fungicide as advised locally

Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.name: Tomato Yellow Leaf Curl Virus
Tomato__Tomato_YellowLeaf__Curl_Virus.description: A virus spread by whiteflies that stunts plants and reduces yield.
symptoms: Leaves curling upward and turning yellow
treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants
Control whiteflies as advised locally
prevention: Use insect nets or reflective mulch

Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.name: Tomato Mosaic Virus
Tomato__Tomato_mosaic_virus.description: A virus that spreads through contact, tools, and contaminated seed.
symptoms: Light and dark green mottled leaves
Slow growth and uneven fruit ripening
treatment: Remove and destroy infected plants (no cure)
Disinfect tools and wash hands
prevention: Avoid handling plants after using tobacco

Tomato_healthy.name: Healthy Tomato Leaf
Tomato_healthy.description: The leaf shows no visible signs of disease.
treatment: No treatment needed
prevention: Water at the base of the plant
Keep the area free of fallen debris
